t.1.157.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While those great-souled Pāṇḍavas were dwelling there in concealment, Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, then came to see them.
t.1.157.2: Seeing him arrive, the scorchers of foes went forth to meet him; bowing down and saluting him, they then stood with joined palms.
t.1.157.4: Do you conduct yourselves according to dharma and the scriptures, O scorchers of foes? Is your reverence toward the brahmins, who are worthy of reverence, not diminished?
t.1.157.3: Having given leave to them all as they sat, the sage, gracious and honored by the Pārthas, spoke these words with affection.
t.1.157.5: Then the blessed seer, having spoken words consonant with dharma and artha and told those various wondrous tales, spoke again as follows.
t.1.157.6: In a forest of austerities there once lived the daughter of a great-souled seer, slender-waisted, with lovely hips and fine brows, endowed with every virtue.
t.1.157.7: Through deeds she herself had done, she became ill-fated; though she was a beautiful maiden, she did not obtain a husband.
t.1.157.8: Then, unhappy, she began to practise austerities for the sake of a husband, and by her fierce austerity, it is said, she pleased Śaṃkara.
t.1.157.9: Pleased with her, the Blessed One said to that ascetic woman, "Choose a boon, good fortune to you, O beautiful lady; I am the giver of boons."
t.1.157.10: Then she spoke to the Lord these words, beneficial to herself, saying again and again, "I desire a husband endowed with every virtue."
t.1.157.11: Then Īśāna Śaṃkara, best of speakers, replied to her thus: "You will have five husbands, good lady."
t.1.157.13: Five times I was addressed by you again with the words "Give me a husband"; when you have gone to another body, that will come to pass just as it was spoken.
t.1.157.12: As she answered Śaṃkara, "Give me one husband," the god spoke to her once more these excellent words.
t.1.157.14: That maiden of divine form, born in the family of Drupada, the blameless Kṛṣṇā Pārṣatī, has been appointed as your wife.
t.1.157.15: Therefore, O mighty ones, enter the city of the Pāñcālas; once you have won her, you will be happy, there is no doubt.
t.1.157.16: Having spoken thus, the illustrious grandfather of the Pāṇḍavas, the one of great austerity, took leave of the Pārthas and Kuntī and departed.
